units.source_text: 六条院源氏也闻知此事。

en.t: Genji of the Rokujo estate also heard about this matter.

units.source_text: 他想：“夕雾为人老成持重，凡事沉着应付，从不受人讥评，

en.t: He thought, "Yugiri is mature and prudent by nature, handles everything calmly, and has never drawn criticism from others,

units.source_text: 一向平安度日，我做父亲的也觉得面目光彩。

en.t: living peacefully all along, so that I, as his father, have felt proud of him.

units.source_text: 回想自己年轻时候，未免稍稍耽好风月，以致流传轻薄之名，且喜他能替我补救。

en.t: When I look back on my own youth, I was rather too fond of love and elegance, and gained a reputation for frivolity, so I was glad that he could make amends for me.

units.source_text: 然而如今发生此事，对任何人都很不利。

en.t: But now that this has happened, it is harmful to everyone concerned.

units.source_text: 对方倘是疏远的人，犹可说也，偏偏又是他的至亲，

en.t: If the woman were someone distant from him, there might still be something to say, but she happens to be one of his closest kin,

units.source_text: 不知前太政大臣对此作何感想。

en.t: and I wonder what the former Grand Minister will think of it.

units.source_text: 这一点夕雾不会不顾虑到，可见前世宿命是不可逃避的了。

en.t: Yugiri cannot have failed to consider that, so it seems that fate from a former life truly cannot be escaped.

units.source_text: 但无论如何，关于此事我不宜插嘴。”

en.t: Still, whatever the case may be, it would not be proper for me to interfere in this matter."

units.source_text: 他觉得此事对落叶公主和云居雁两皆不利，故闻讯之后，不胜愁叹。

en.t: He felt that the affair was harmful both to Princess Ochiba and to Kumoi no Kari, and after hearing the news he was overcome with sorrow and sighs.

units.source_text: 他自己回想过去之事，推量未来之状，便对紫夫人表示：看到落叶公主丧夫的事例，不免担心自己身后之事。

en.t: Reflecting on his own past and imagining what might come in the future, he told Lady Murasaki that seeing Princess Ochiba widowed made him anxious about what would happen after his own death.

units.source_text: 紫夫人面红了，自念我死了丈夫难道会久留在世么，便觉心情不快。

en.t: Lady Murasaki blushed and thought to herself that, if her husband died, surely she would not remain long in this world, and the thought left her unhappy.

units.source_text: 她想：“女人持身之难，苦患之多，世间无出其右了！

en.t: She thought, "Nothing in the world surpasses the difficulty of a woman's conduct and the many sufferings she must bear.

units.source_text: 如果对于悲哀之情、欢乐之趣，一概漠不关心，只管韬晦沉默，

en.t: If one were indifferent to every feeling of sorrow and every pleasure of joy, and merely hid oneself away in silence,

units.source_text: 那么安得享受世间荣华之乐、慰藉人生无常之苦呢？

en.t: how could one ever enjoy the splendor of the world or console oneself for the pain of life's impermanence?

units.source_text: 况且一个女子无知无识，形同白痴，岂不辜负父母养育之恩而使他们伤心失望呢？

en.t: Besides, if a woman is ignorant and senseless, almost like a fool, would she not betray the care with which her parents raised her and make them grieve in disappointment?

units.source_text: 万事隐藏在心中，像古代寓言中所谓无言太子，

en.t: To hide everything within one's heart, like the so-called Silent Prince of ancient fable,

units.source_text: 即僧人所引为苦难之典型者，明知世事孰善孰恶，却将意见埋藏胸底，毕竟也太乏味了。

en.t: the figure whom monks cite as an example of suffering, and to know clearly what is good and bad in worldly affairs yet bury one's opinions deep in the breast, is after all far too dreary.

units.source_text: 虽然心由自主，却不知道如何才能保持恰到好处。”

en.t: Although one's heart is one's own, I do not know how one can keep it in proper balance."

units.source_text: 如此左思右想，并非为了自己，只是为了大公主的前途。

en.t: As she turned these thoughts over again and again, it was not for her own sake, but only for the future of the elder princess.
